lots.title: Maintenance and extension of the Operational Windstorm Service
lots.description: Maintain and further develop the C3S Operational Windstorm Service for professional users (insurance, reinsurance, climate risk). Scope includes ongoing operation of the ERA5-based windstorm tracks and footprints dataset, maintenance of its two prototype applications and associated Jupyter Notebooks, preparation for migration to ERA6, geographic extension to Northern Hemisphere (and where feasible Southern Hemisphere) midlatitudes, extension of variables and indicators (cumulated precipitation, return periods), enhancement of windstorm statistics for catastrophe modelling (including UNSEEN-type resampling, synthetic events, AI-based methods), development of extra-tropical storm indicators for reanalysis and climate projections (CMIP6/CMIP7, CORDEX), consistency with C3S Atlas, user engagement and co-development of online demonstrators, training/dissemination, coordination with Lot 2, Level-2 user support, and contribution to the ESOTC report.
requirements: Maintain the CDS dataset 'Windstorm tracks and footprints derived from reanalysis over Europe between 1940 to present' and its downscaled ~1 km footprint product.
Maintain the two prototype applications so they remain fully operational, are updated when underlying datasets change, and are promptly restored after technical issues.
Maintain associated Jupyter Notebooks supporting advanced and expert users of the windstorm dataset.
Perform ongoing operational maintenance, monitoring, troubleshooting and timely updates of the above products.
Review, validate and where necessary correct post-processing and spatial filtering applied to ETC diagnostics so high-impact European windstorms are not inadvertently excluded.
Perform scientific completeness and consistency checks, including validation against known recent high-impact European windstorms.
Assess the implications of the diagnostics for use in climate assessment products, in particular the C3S European State of the Climate (ESOTC).

Explore, test and benchmark AI-based methods for identification, tracking and characterisation of extra-tropical cyclones and associated windstorms with the objective of reproducing the existing algorithm-based diagnostics; any AI approach must be physically consistent, fully documented and rigorously evaluated against the current ERA5-based methodology before operational consideration.
Provide Level 2 user support, responding to user queries escalated by the C3S User Support team.

Prepare the migration of the CDS catalogue entry and associated workflows to ERA6, including targeted testing of storm detection/tracking/post-processing with initial ERA6 data and sensitivity assessment.

Extend the service geographically beyond the current European domain to the Northern Hemisphere midlatitudes and, where technically and scientifically feasible, Southern Hemisphere midlatitudes, ensuring methodological consistency while accounting for regional storm differences.
Add cumulated precipitation associated with windstorm events as complementary hazard information alongside wind gusts.
Introduce return period estimates for key variables relevant to windstorm risk, with methodological consistency and suitability for risk assessment applications.
Design delivery so products are well suited for the downstream community (e.g. insurance premium review cycles).

Enhance windstorm statistics for downstream risk and catastrophe modelling; increase effective sample size of windstorm events using resampling (e.g. UNSEEN-type), synthetic windstorm events, perturbation/analogue approaches and/or AI-based generative methods, benchmarking against the existing ERA5-based dataset.

Develop and assess extra-tropical storm indicators derived from reanalysis (ERA5/ERA6) and climate projection datasets (CMIP6/CMIP7 when available, CORDEX), usable without requiring explicit tracking of individual storms, based on gridded/regional diagnostics such as exceedance metrics, spatial aggregates, persistence or footprint-based indicators.
Ensure methodological consistency with Copernicus Climate Change Service Atlas products in terms of selected climate models, with methods adaptable to evolving background models and ensembles.

Develop a user engagement strategy identifying relevant user communities (insurance/reinsurance, catastrophe modelling community, EIOPA or equivalent policymakers), and co-develop real case studies and online demonstrators with champion users and ECMWF.
Deliver case-study findings (positive and negative) and lessons learned / best practices for the insurance and risk-assessment sector.

Transform value-adding case studies into online demonstrators that deliver regularly updated operational products, include a visual component co-designed with users, expose the underlying dataset via the CDS in an automatically maintainable way, and provide complete documentation of workflows and methodologies.

Co-design dissemination materials, training elements and EQC content with champion users and ECMWF, supporting ECMWF training, MOOCs and train-the-trainer activities, and liaising with the C3S Evaluation and Quality Control (EQC) contractor.
Set up and maintain content for a C3S website providing a continuously updated web presence for the service.
Ensure coordination and technical consistency with Lot 2, particularly for storm-surge related hazards and joint windstorm-storm surge products (see Section 6).

Propose a coherent set of deliverables that achieve the key outcomes, following Section 7.3 guidance, each with an associated resource allocation (person-months and financial budget) summing to the requested payroll budget.

Comply with all cross-cutting general requirements in Section 7 (Implementation Schedule, WP0 Management & Coordination, Code delivery & documentation aligned with the ECMWF Codex, L2 user support, ESOTC contribution, Communication, KPIs, Payment Plan, Tender format in Section 8).
Contribute to the ESOTC report where products are selected for inclusion in a section, per Section 7.6 (treated as optional tasks, triggered by ECMWF).

Propose SMART KPIs covering system performance (e.g. uptime, response time), search effectiveness (e.g. match rate of search results to CDS datasets/resources), and user satisfaction, to be refined with ECMWF in the first 6 months.

lots.title: Maintenance and extension of operational storm surge products
lots.description: Ensure continued operational delivery, scientific robustness and strategic extension of the Operational Storm Surge Climate Service under C3S. Scope includes operational running and NRT updating of the reanalysis-based storm surge / extreme sea-level products (currently derived from a Global Tide and Surge Model with ERA5 forcing), QA/QC procedures, ERA6 migration preparation, exploration of AI-based methods (surrogates, post-processing, hybrid approaches), maintenance and evolution of indicators (percentiles, return periods, confidence intervals), restructuring the climate-projections component to a broad CMIP6 (and CMIP7 when available) ensemble aligned with the C3S Atlas philosophy, coordination with Lot 1 for joint windstorm-storm surge products, training, Level-2 support, C3S web content, and ESOTC contribution.
requirements: Generate an operational chain to update the current reanalysis-based storm-surge product with NRT delivery, ensuring continuous operational delivery at least of the same quality and resolution as current products, with monitoring and timely restoration after issues.

Tenderers may propose alternative modelling frameworks or updated model versions provided outputs are scientifically equivalent or improved, methodological changes are fully documented, and historical-consistency, uncertainty and interpretation impacts are clearly assessed; any change of underlying model is subject to scientific validation, benchmarking against existing products and prior ECMWF/C3S approval.
Implement an operational update cycle with updates at least monthly (or as agreed with ECMWF/C3S) to incorporate newly available reanalysis data and keep the catalogue current.

Implement QA/QC procedures appropriate for operational dissemination: consistency checks, completeness checks, outlier detection, metadata validation, and verification against known historical high-water events where feasible.
Maintain and update CDS catalogue entries, documentation and user guidance so changes are traceable and reproducible.

Prepare the product chain for ERA6, including forcing/resolution/availability impact assessment, targeted 'early ERA6' testing of the end-to-end workflow (forcing → modelling/post-processing → delivery), documented sensitivity assessment and migration plan.

Explore AI-based methods for generation, emulation, acceleration or post-processing of storm surge and extreme sea-level products (surrogate/emulation models for hydrodynamic simulations, AI-assisted post-processing/bias correction/downscaling, hybrid physical/ML approaches); any AI method shall be physically consistent, rigorously evaluated, assessed for operational robustness, and must not compromise continuity or reliability.

Maintain the indicator generation chain (downstream processing, delivery, validation and documentation) for statistical indicators (e.g. percentiles, return periods with confidence bounds) for total water levels and surge levels.
Ensure indicators remain consistent across updates (versioning, methodological traceability, backward compatibility where possible).
Provide clear documentation of methods, assumptions, limitations and uncertainty treatment (extreme value methodology, confidence intervals, sensitivity to record length).
Expand on the indicators if needed by the user community.
Coordinate with Lot 1 and ensure technical consistency for relevant joint products and related hazards (see Section 6).

Restructure the projections component so storm-surge / sea-level indicators can be produced and assessed from a broad selection of CMIP6 simulations in the CDS up to 2100 and CMIP7 simulations when they become available, robust to evolving model availability and ensemble composition.

Align the projections component with the C3S Atlas philosophy: transparent model selection rules, consistent periods/scenarios (near-term/mid-century/end-century), robust ensemble statistics, and reproducible processing.

Define and document a model/ensemble selection strategy (eligibility criteria, scenario coverage, temporal windows, handling of multiple realizations) and a consistent approach for ensemble aggregation and uncertainty characterisation (model spread, internal variability proxies, robustness metrics consistent with Atlas practices).

Ensure methodological consistency and traceability between historical reanalysis indicators (ERA5/ERA6) and future indicators derived from CMIP ensembles, including clear separation of drivers (mean sea level vs surge/tide variability) where relevant.
Design indicators and their subset of users/use cases in co-definition with C3S.
Provide updated training and example workflows (e.g. notebooks demonstrating retrieval, visualisation, detrending, percentile/return-period calculations and interpretation).
Provide Level-2 support when escalated by the C3S User Support function.
Set up and provide content (text, tools, materials) for a C3S website providing a continuously updated web presence for the service.
Contribute to the ESOTC report writing if products are included in a specific section (see Section 7.6), treated as optional tasks triggered by ECMWF.
Propose a coherent set of deliverables that achieve the key outcomes, per Section 7.3.

Comply with all cross-cutting general requirements in Section 7 (Implementation Schedule, WP0, ECMWF Codex for code delivery, L2 support, Communication, KPIs, Payment Plan, Tender format in Section 8).
